problems.form_value: A custom online system guided participants' interactions with GenAI during one creative phase, depending on the arm: idea generation (brainstorming, ideas supplied) or idea elaboration (refining the participant's own ideas).
problems.source_says: Minor. Study 3 never says what ChatGPT did in either phase. The text says only that a custom system guided interactions with GenAI during specific phases. It also says that the phase materials were adapted from Mannucci and Perry-Smith (2022), consistent with Study 2, whose instructions only allow participants 'to collaborate with the GenAI tool' (Appendices E-F). The Study 3 phase instructions are not printed: Appendix H gives only the intelligence news excerpts. A text-layer search finds 'brainstorm' only in the Study 1 quotes (pp. 5, 12), the practical implications (p. 10), and a reference title (p. 15), and finds 'supplied' nowhere. So 'brainstorming, ideas supplied' has no support. The elaboration gloss rests on Study 2 by analogy. Suggested wording: 'idea generation (collaborating with ChatGPT while conceiving initial ideas) or idea elaboration (collaborating while elaborating them); the Study 3 phase instructions are not printed.' The role code 'other' stands, and criterion 1 is not affected.
problems.quote: To standardize human–GenAI collaboration, we developed a custom online system that guided participants’ interactions with GenAI during specific creative phases (Chen & Chan, 2024).
problems.locator: p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 14, Appendix H; p. 13, Appendices E-F; text-layer search of pp. 1-16 for brainstorm*, suppl*

problems.form_value: each participant writes two product proposals, one with the SparkDesk LLM allowed in one 10-minute phase (idea generation in 2a, idea elaboration in 2b) and one without AI, in randomized order
problems.source_says: Minor. The paper names SparkDesk only in the Study 2a procedures (p. 5). For Study 2b the text says 'GenAI' and Appendix F says 'the GenAI tool'. The form's own studies[S3].ai_tool.name_model and its reconciliation record the tool as not named for 2b, so the summary contradicts both. Suggested wording: 'one with a GenAI tool allowed in one 10-minute phase (SparkDesk, named for 2a only; idea generation in 2a, idea elaboration in 2b)'. Criterion 1 is not affected, because the paper calls the Study 2b tool GenAI.
problems.quote: A key distinction lay in task execution: in one task, participants collaborated with GenAI during the idea elaboration phase, whereas in the other, they worked independently (see Appendix F).
problems.locator: p. 6, Section 5.2.1; p. 13, Appendix F; p. 5, Section 5.1.1 (SparkDesk named for Study 2a)

confirmed.statement: Study 2a states a random order within person: 'Both the task order and the human–GenAI collaboration order were randomized to control for order effects.' The paper calls the design within-subjects. Checks (a) and (e) hold, and randomized = yes, unit = within_person_order, structure = within are right. The form's quote is verbatim and its locator is right.

Study 2b states its randomization only by reference: 'The randomization procedures in Study 2b were identical to those used in Study 2a.' The paper also calls it a within-subjects design. This supports randomized = yes and a random order of conditions and tasks (checks a and e). The form's quote is verbatim and its locator is right.

Study 3 states random assignment: 'A randomized 2 × 2 between-subjects design assigned participants to one of four experimental conditions.' The factors are creative phase (idea generation vs idea elaboration) and perceived GenAI intelligence (high vs low). randomized = yes, unit = individual, and structure = between are right, and check (e) does not apply. The form's quote is verbatim. A text-layer search of all 16 pages finds no other statement on allocation.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 6.1; text-layer search of pp. 1-16 for random*, assign*, counterbalanc*, within-subjects, between-subjects

confirmed.statement: What was assigned is access to generative AI for the participant's own scored work (check b). In Studies 2a and 2b the AI condition allows participants 'to collaborate with the GenAI tool' in one 10-minute phase of their own product proposal. The H condition bars 'search engines or tools like GenAI' in both phases. In Study 3 all four cells work with ChatGPT on their own advertising proposal, and the cells differ in the collaboration phase and in the intelligence framing. Three blind marketing experts rate each participant's own proposal in Study 2, and Study 3 uses the same approach. So the conditions do not differ only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 13, Appendix E; pp. 13-14, Appendix F; p. 5, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.2; p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; p. 14, Appendix G

confirmed.statement: The tools are generative AI (check c). Study 2a uses SparkDesk, 'a Chinese-developed cognitive intelligence large language model (LLM)'. Study 3 uses ChatGPT through a custom system linked by an API. Study 2b names no tool and says only GenAI ('the GenAI tool'). The form records this correctly in studies[S3].ai_tool.name_model.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 5.1.1; p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 6, Section 5.2.1; p. 13, Appendix F

confirmed.statement: The comparison arms match the form (check d). In 2a and 2b the H condition works without GenAI or search engines in both phases (ai = none, ai_vs_bau). Study 3 has no no-AI arm, and its phase contrast compares two GenAI configurations (ai_design), which the codebook's 'ideas versus refinement' example covers. The phase manipulation check is t(196) = 28.63, p < 0.001 (generation M = 6.31, elaboration M = 2.00).
confirmed.locator: p. 13, Appendix E; pp. 13-14, Appendix F; p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 8, Section 6.3.2

confirmed.statement: The Study 3 arm descriptions follow the paper: ChatGPT in one of two 10-minute phases, and a news excerpt plus a recall task for the intelligence factor, which the paper points to Appendix H for. The form says correctly that the paper does not state whether ChatGPT was blocked in the phase that was not assigned.
Preregistration is right. Only Study 3 links an AsPredicted plan (https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf). The paper says nothing about preregistration for Studies 2a and 2b, so not_stated fits.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 6.1; text-layer search of pp. 1-16 for AsPredicted

confirmed.statement: No count at assignment is printed. Each study gives recruits and attention-check exclusions (45 to 42, 45 to 44, 205 to 198) without saying whether the exclusions came before or after assignment. Study 3 gives no cell sizes. So n_randomized = null is right, and the form's exclusion notes are right.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 5.1.1; p. 6, Section 5.2.1; p. 7, Section 6.1; p. 8, Table 3 (CP M = 0.49)

confirmed.statement: No balance test is reported for Study 3. The only evidence is Table 3: the phase dummy (CP) correlates −0.01 with gender, 0.19** with age, −0.01 with education, and −0.10 with industry. Its correlations with digital skills (−0.14*) and creative self-efficacy (−0.15*) involve scales taken after the task. The age imbalance deserves a note, but it does not contradict the stated random assignment.
confirmed.locator: p. 8, Table 3 (page rendered at 4x); p. 7, Section 6.1 (measures taken upon completing the task)

summary: The PDF states random assignment for every experiment the form calls randomized: a random order within person in Study 2a (p. 5) and, by reference, Study 2b (p. 6), where GenAI is allowed in one phase of the participant's own proposal versus no GenAI, and a randomized 2 × 2 between-subjects design in Study 3 (p. 7) that varies the phase of ChatGPT collaboration, so criterion 1 holds through Study 3 (198 analyzed, an ai_design contrast). The coding is refuted only in detail: Study 3's how_used says ChatGPT supplied ideas through brainstorming, which the paper never states, and the paper_design_summary names SparkDesk for Study 2b, where the paper names no tool.
